reading.title: Before the ceremony
reading.text: Salma arrives early for her adult graduation ceremony. An organizer checks the stage, podium and microphone. Salma has prepared a short speech. Later, she will receive her diploma and may greet the presenter with a handshake. The procession brings graduates into the hall, and the recessional takes them out at the end. The audience offers applause. Music accompanies the entrance. Salma wears an academic cap and gown. The cap has a tassel. An honor cord and a stole mark distinctions at her institution, but their colors do not have a universal meaning. She follows the organizer’s instructions rather than guessing from another university’s photographs.

reading.title: Looking back together
reading.text: At a reunion after commencement, adult alumni remember their alma mater. A display includes a sash, dress shoes and a class ring. Someone shows a pin and medal, while a photograph recalls a cap toss at an earlier event. This year the group chooses a class photo instead. A yearbook includes memories of speakers. The glossary explains valedictorian and salutatorian as titles used in some US schools, commonly linked to academic rank and speeches. It also explains honors and cum laude. The alumni learn that recognition rules vary. They do not assume every school uses the same titles or selects speakers in the same way.
